openLog.observations: Heading, printed-page line, opening wave discussion, historical-model paragraphs and start of the tourmaline explanation are readable. Paragraph spacing and section separator are clear. The lower-edge continuation is covered by tile 2.

Tourmaline prose continues without a gap. Figure 208 is resolved and its plate, arrows, rotation cue and all four English labels are readable; caption 208 is clear. Two-crystal prose and a/b/c references are readable. Figure 209 continues into tile 3.

All three figure 209 subpanels are resolved. Aligned, turning and crossed headings, numbered plates and axis views, output labels and caption 209 are readable without label collisions. The two-facts paragraph and bold longitudinal-wave passage continue correctly into tile 4.

Longitudinal-wave conclusion, two-hypothesis transition, bold transverse-wave statement, water-wave discussion and natural-light explanation are readable with consistent flow. Bold text wraps cleanly. Figure 210 begins at the lower edge and is fully covered by tile 5.

Figures 210 and 211, their direction labels, plane p and captions are resolved and legible. The second hypothesis, polarization terminology and polarizer/analyzer passages are readable. Inline p and 90-degree expressions render clearly without raw markup, overlap or vertical clipping.

Projection and polarization prose continues into the mechanical analogy without missing text. Figure 212 is resolved at its native left scroll position: changing-directions label, moving-end label, rope, first box and vertical opening are visible and readable. Right-edge fragments of offscreen labels are expected scroll-window boundaries, not covered-label passes.

Figure 212's lower left-visible continuation and caption are preserved. Post-figure 90-degree prose, historical polarizing-sheet discussion, decimal 0.1 and color caveat are readable. The historical car-light discussion starts in the lower portion and continues into tile 8. Boundary-truncated figure-212 sentence labels remain excluded.

The final historical car-light discussion, inline 45-degree expression, road-reflection caveat and last non-recommendation sentence are readable through their endings. The visible zero-question footer button is legible and does not overlap the prose. Remaining visible space is ordinary bottom spacing, not missing content.
